facts.raw_span: A 15-year-old boy with biopsy-proven Crohn disease
infiximab therapy (5 mg/kg subcutaneous injection every 8 weeks)
later switched to adalimumab (40-mg/0.8-mL subcutaneous injection every 2 weeks) due to disease relapse
Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids
Both lower eyelids were ectropic
Visual acuity was 20/20 OU
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
Diffuse conjunctival hyperemia
Rest of the ophthalmic examination was unremarkable
A 15-year-old boy with biopsy-proven Crohn disease
infiximab therapy (5 mg/kg subcutaneous injection every 8 weeks)
later switched to adalimumab (40-mg/0.8-mL subcutaneous injection every 2 weeks) due to disease relapse
Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids
Both lower eyelids were ectropic
Visual acuity was 20/20 OU
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
Diffuse conjunctival hyperemia
Rest of the ophthalmic examination was unremarkable

concepts.why: Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids and crusty plaques on the eyelid margins suggest blepharitis
Both lower eyelids were ectropic, which is a sign of ectropion
Biopsy-proven Crohn disease is a clear indication of the disease
Ocular symptoms such as blepharitis, ectropion, and conjunctivitis can be extraintestinal manifestations of Crohn disease
The patient developed ocular inflammation after switching to adalimumab, suggesting a possible association between the medication and the symptoms
It explains the finding of crusty plaques on the eyelid margins and diffuse conjunctival hyperemia in the context of normal visual acuity.

rationales.F01: Crohn disease is a known risk factor for extraintestinal manifestations.
rationales.F02: Infliximab is a TNF-alpha inhibitor that can cause ocular inflammation.
rationales.F03: Adalimumab is another TNF-alpha inhibitor that can cause ocular inflammation.
rationales.F04: Blepharitis is characterized by scaly, thickened, and erythematous eyelids.
rationales.F05: Ectropion is characterized by outward turning of the eyelid margin.
rationales.F07: Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins are a common finding in blepharitis.
rationales.F08: Diffuse conjunctival hyperemia is a common finding in conjunctivitis.
